topic.label: Philosophy
topic.desc: Philosophy: rigorous inquiry into knowledge, reality, mind, value, reasoning and the history of these questions.

concepts: Formal and informal reasoning: propositional and predicate logic, validity, proof and fallacies.
The nature, sources and limits of knowledge, justification, belief and scepticism.
The nature of reality: existence, identity, causation, time, modality and free will.
Consciousness, mental content, the mind-body problem, meaning and reference.
Normative ethics, metaethics and applied ethics, including consequentialism, deontology and virtue.
History of Philosophy and Political Philosophy
Major figures and traditions from ancient to contemporary, and theories of justice, rights and the state.
skills: Translates natural language arguments into propositional or predicate logic and checks validity with a truth table or derivation.
Constructs natural deduction proofs and checks each line cites a valid rule.
Identifies informal fallacies in texts and checks each label against a standard definition and the passage.
Classifies a view as foundationalist, coherentist or reliabilist and checks the classification against its primary text.
Constructs counterexamples to analyses of knowledge and checks each case meets the analysis but intuitively fails.
Reconstructs sceptical arguments premise by premise and checks responses address a specific premise.
Identifies what entities a theory commits to and checks the claim using quantifier paraphrase.
Sets out the cases and intuitions in a thought experiment and checks the conclusion follows from them.
Maps compatibilist, libertarian and hard determinist positions on a question and checks each against cited sources.
Reconstructs arguments for dualism and physicalism in standard form and checks premise dependence.
Applies descriptivist and causal theories of reference to cases and checks predictions against the case facts.
Evaluates claims about machine consciousness and understanding and checks each claim against named criteria.
Applies consequentialist, deontological and virtue analyses to a case and checks each verdict follows from the theory.
Writes balanced briefs on bioethics or technology ethics questions and checks both sides are stated at full strength.
Classifies a position as realist, expressivist or error theoretic and checks against the author text.
Explains a passage from a primary text in context and checks the reading against the original language and scholarship.
Compares theories of justice such as Rawls and Nozick on a policy question and checks fidelity to each text.
Finds journal articles on a debate and checks each citation exists and supports the attributed claim.
mcp: Enhance responses with scholarly research and citations
Translate text and documents across 100+ languages, with your preferred styles applied
